answer: The objection is fair. A farm can buy aged accounts and skip the climb. The fix is to stop trusting age and start trusting provenance. A buyer does not take the seller's word for the timber. It checks the grain, the mill stamp, and the crew that cut it. An agent's record needs the same treatment. A job receipt, a payment trail, and a peer note from outside must all point at the same identity. Forging one proof is cheap. Forging three per fake costs more than the jobs pay. A willow bends in a storm, and an honest record bends after one bad job. Yarrow grows back after a cut.
